title: One-block pump at the epoch bell
teach: Two quiet epochs, then a giant buy in the last minute before the close. The epoch does close expansion, so fees route that way — but the multiplier reads the two previously closed epochs, not this one. A single-block pump cannot buy a raise; at most it skips one cut. This is the one-epoch case only: a pump sustained across consecutive epochs does move m, and `pnpm attack` measures what that costs (see A3, and the adversarial probes in packages/engine/src/adversary.ts).

actions.note: two quiet epochs, both close at F = 0
